match.reason: No existing point covers why people start a business and how they weigh their skills, money and risk first; entrepreneurship and innovation is a related but broader idea about risk-taking and competition.

draft.title: The decision to start a business
card: People start a business for different reasons. Some want to be their own boss and make their own decisions.
Others want to follow an idea or interest, or to earn more than they could as an employee. Earning more is not guaranteed.
Before starting, an owner weighs up their skills, their money and the risk. Skills mean what they can do or learn. Money means what they can put in and live on.
Risk is the chance the business does not work and the owner loses money or time. A person may start only if the possible gain seems worth that risk.
draft.remember: Starting a business is a choice made by weighing reasons for it against skills, money and risk.

a.q: Which is a reason a person might choose to start a business?
opts: To be their own boss and make their own decisions
To avoid all risk of losing money
To be sure of earning more than an employee
To have no need for any skills
a.why: Being your own boss is a common reason to start. Starting a business does not remove risk, and extra earnings are not guaranteed, so the other options are wrong.
a.clue: Which reason is about independence, not a promise?

b.q: Sam is a skilled baker in Orange. He has a new recipe idea but only a little savings. Which step best shows he is weighing the decision to start a bakery?
opts: Checking whether his savings could cover costs and losses
Quitting his job straight away to save time
Assuming the bakery will earn more than his wage
Ignoring risk because his recipe is good
b.why: Sam is weighing his money against the risk of losses. Quitting at once or assuming higher earnings skips the weighing. A good idea does not remove risk.
b.clue: Weighing means comparing money and risk before acting.

a.best: To be their own boss and make their own decisions

b.best: Checking whether his savings could cover costs and losses

problems.detail: "A person may start only if the possible gain seems worth that risk" can read as a rule about when someone is allowed to start a business. A clearer version would be "A person may decide to start if the possible gain seems worth that risk."
